speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you are suffering from sudden-onset lower back pain radiating down your leg; can you tell me if this pain travels all the way to your foot or just stops at your knee?

Also, have you noticed any numbness, tingling, or weakness in that specific leg?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lumbar Radiculopathy (likely L5 or S1 nerve root compression) secondary to acute onset event, possibly a slipped disc or muscle strain given the sudden onset after exercise and radiation to the foot.

Given the radiation to the foot, I need to confirm if you have any trouble lifting your big toe or standing on your toes, which would indicate specific nerve weakness. Have you experienced any bowel or bladder changes recently?
